349986.title: Consistency conjecture for adjacent distance graphs
349986.statement: Let $n\geq 1$ be a number. Let $\Delta_n$ be the graph on $\mathbb{R}^n$ connecting points of rational Euclidean distance. The **adjacent distance-graph consistency conjecture.** The statement that the chromatic number of $\Delta_n$ is countable while that of $\Delta_{n+1}$ is not is consistent with $\mathrm{ZF}+\mathrm{DC}$. This concerns the possibility of separating the chromatic behavior of consecutive distance graphs in choiceless set theory; the conjecture is still open for $n=4$ and higher.

350085.title: The heroic forbidden-set conjecture for oriented forests and heroes
350085.statement:
Let $H$ be a hero, meaning a tournament such that every tournament not containing $H$ has bounded dichromatic number, and let $F$ be an oriented forest. A set of digraphs is **heroic** if every digraph with none of its members as an induced subdigraph has bounded dichromatic number. **The heroic forbidden-set conjecture.** The set $\{\overleftrightarrow{K_2},H,F\}$ is heroic if and only if either $F$ is the disjoint union of oriented stars or $H$ is a transitive tournament.

This is presented as an analogue of the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture for oriented graphs. The only-if direction was proved in the cited prior work, while the conjecture is stated to be widely open.

350166.title: Generic existence conjecture for basic WKB cameral networks
350166.statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be the Hitchin base. A **basic WKB cameral network** associated to $a\in\mathcal A$ consists of a suitable homotopy-equivalent open subset of the curve together with finitely many labelled Stokes curves and their joints, as in the WKB construction. **Generic existence conjecture.** With respect to the classical topology, there is a dense open set $U\subset\mathcal A$ such that every $a\in U$ has an associated basic WKB cameral network. The conjecture would establish generic existence of finite WKB cameral networks; the supplied text does not state that it has been proved.

350189.title: Spinoza–West sharp threshold conjecture for connectedness recognition
350189.statement: Let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph, and let $\mathcal{D}_\ell(G)$ be the multiset of all induced subgraphs of $G$ on $\ell$ vertices. The connectedness of $G$ is **determined by** $\mathcal{D}_\ell(G)$ if any two $n$-vertex graphs with the same $\ell$-deck are either both connected or both disconnected. **Spinoza–West connectedness conjecture.** For $n\geq 6$ and $\ell\geq\lfloor n/2\rfloor+1$, the connectedness of an $n$-vertex graph $G$ is determined by $\mathcal{D}_\ell(G)$, and this threshold is sharp. The threshold is motivated by non-isomorphic connected and disconnected graphs with identical $\ell$-decks for $\ell\leq\lfloor n/2\rfloor$; the supplied status evidence records a later result of Spinoza and West with a different sufficient range, so this conjecture is marked solved.

350311.title: The forbidden-subdiagram characterization conjecture for k-terminal-minimality
350311.statement: A chord diagram is **$k$-terminal-minimal** if it is $k$-terminal and minimal with respect to that property under the reduction considered in the paper. **The forbidden-subdiagram characterization conjecture.** There is a nice infinite forbidden-subdiagram characterization of $k$-terminal-minimality. The source presents this as a preliminary expectation and gives no precise forbidden family or proof, so the conjecture remains open.

350420.title: Conjectured relative clique number of planar graphs of girth at least 3
350420.statement:
Let $m,n$ be nonnegative integers, let $\mathcal{P}_3$ be the family of planar graphs of girth at least $3$, and let $\omega_{a(m,n)}$ and $\omega_{r(m,n)}$ denote the $(m,n)$-absolute and $(m,n)$-relative clique numbers, respectively.

**Planar girth-three conjecture.** For the family $\mathcal{P}_3$ of planar graphs,

$$
\omega_{a(m,n)}({\mathcal{P}_3}) = \omega_{r(m,n)}({\mathcal{P}_3})=3(2m+n)^2 + (2m+n) +1.
$$

The authors state this as a tight bound for planar graphs of girth at least $3$, strengthening an earlier conjecture of Bensmail, Duffy, and Sen that concerned only the $(m,n)$-absolute clique number. The source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

350421.title: Conjectured relative clique number of triangle-free planar graphs
350421.statement:
Let $m,n$ be nonnegative integers, let $\mathcal{P}_4$ be the family of triangle-free planar graphs, and let $\omega_{r(m,n)}$ denote the $(m,n)$-relative clique number.

**Triangle-free planar conjecture.** For the family $\mathcal{P}_4$ of triangle-free planar graphs,

$$
\omega_{r(m,n)}({\mathcal{P}_4})=2(2m+n)^2 +2.
$$

The authors present this as a tight conjectural value for the relative clique number; the corresponding absolute clique number is already known exactly. The source provides no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.

350432.title: Uniqueness conjecture for cograph minimal $(\infty,k)$-polar obstructions
350432.statement:
A **cograph minimal $(\infty,k)$-polar obstruction** is a cograph that is not $(\infty,k)$-polar but whose every proper induced subgraph is $(\infty,k)$-polar; its **type** $(c,i)$ records its number $c$ of connected components and its number $i$ of isolated vertices. For integers $k,c,i$ satisfying

$$
1\leq i\leq c-2\leq k,
$$

**Uniqueness conjecture.** There exists exactly one cograph minimal $(\infty,k)$-polar obstruction of type $(c,i)$. This extends the cases for which uniqueness is established and leaves the remaining admissible types to be characterized.

350476.title: Beaton–Brown–Cameron conjecture on independence equivalence of odd cycles
350476.statement:
Let $n\geq 4$ be odd, let $C_n$ be the cyclic graph on $n$ vertices, and let $D_n$ be the graph shown in Figure~. Two graphs are **independence equivalent** when they have the same independence polynomial.

**Beaton–Brown–Cameron conjecture.** If $3\not\vert n$, then a graph $G$ is independence equivalent to $C_n$ if and only if

$$
G\in\{C_n,D_n\}.
$$

This conjecture asks for a complete description of the independence equivalence class of $C_n$ for odd $n\geq 4$ not divisible by $3$. The cited results establish the analogous classification for even $n\geq 4$, except $n=6$, and for prime powers $n=p^k$ with $p\geq 5$ prime; the stated odd-cycle case remains open here.

350599.title: Nonvanishing leading-term conjecture for the elliptic graph-complex classes
350599.statement: For $n\geq0$, let $t_{2n}$ be the loop-free graph with $2n+2$ vertices described in the source, and let $\delta_{2n}\in\mathfrak{r}^{\mathrm{non-fr}}_{(1)}$ be Enriquez's derivation. Under the stated isomorphism between the graph-complex cohomology and the non-framed Grothendieck–Teichmüller Lie algebra, **the leading-term conjecture.** The element $\delta_{2n}$ corresponds to a graph cohomology class every representative of which has a nonzero coefficient of $t_{2n}$. The source constructs closed nonexact classes with these tree parts and proposes this correspondence; no resolution is stated.

350643.title: Decidability of the word problem for Gray categories and braided monoidal categories
350643.statement: Let the word problem for 3-cells of Gray categories be the problem of deciding whether two such cells are equal, and likewise let the word problem for cells of braided monoidal categories be the problem of deciding whether two such cells are equal. **Decidability conjecture.** The word problem for 3-cells of Gray categories, and hence for cells of braided monoidal categories, is decidable. The paper establishes that these word problems are at least as hard as the unknotting problem; no algorithm for the braided monoidal word problem is known to date, so decidability remains open.

350663.title: Basso–Dixon fishnet determinant conjecture
350663.statement:
For integers $n\geq m\geq2$, let $\overline{G}_{m,n}$ be the $m$-row, $n$-column fishnet graph and let $f_{\overline{G}_{m,n}}(z)$ denote its graphical function. Define the $m\times m$ Hankel matrix $H=(H_{i,j})_{i,j=1,\ldots,m}$ by

$$
H_{i,j}(z)=(n-m+i+j-2)!(n-m+i+j-1)!f_{\overline{G}_{1,n-m+i+j-1}}(z).
$$

**Basso–Dixon fishnet determinant conjecture.**

$$
f_{\overline{G}_{m,n}}(z)=\frac{\det H(z)}{\displaystyle\prod_{k=n-m}^{n+m-1}k!}.
$$

This conjecture gives all rectangular fishnet graphical functions with $n\geq m\geq2$ in terms of the one-row ladder functions. The one-row case is known, but the supplied text describes the general fishnets as unsolved and gives no resolution of the determinant formula.

350693.title: Coroničová Hurajová–Gago–Madaras blow-up conjecture for betweenness-uniform graphs
350693.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on vertex set $\{v_1,\dots,v_n\}$, and let $G[H_1,\dots,H_n]$ denote the graph obtained by replacing each vertex $v_i$ with a graph $H_i$ and adding all edges prescribed by the edges of $G$. A graph is **betweenness-uniform** when all its vertices have the same betweenness.

**Coroničová Hurajová–Gago–Madaras conjecture.** For any graph $G$ on a vertex set $\{v_1,\dots,v_n\}$ there exist graphs $H_1,\dots,H_n$ such that $G[H_1,\dots,H_n]$ is betweenness-uniform.

The conjecture proposes that every graph admits a suitable blow-up yielding a betweenness-uniform graph. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.

350802.title: The DCI and CI classification conjecture for dihedral groups
350802.statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer and let $\mathrm{D}_{2n}$ be the dihedral group of order $2n$. A finite group is a **DCI-group** if every Cayley digraph on it is a CI-digraph, and a **CI-group** if every Cayley graph on it is a CI-graph. **Dihedral DCI and CI classification conjecture.** The group $\mathrm{D}_{2n}$ is a DCI-group if and only if $n=2$ or $n$ is odd-square-free, and $\mathrm{D}_{2n}$ is a CI-group if and only if $n=2,9$ or $n$ is odd-square-free. The preceding corollary establishes the necessity of these conditions; the conjecture asserts the converse.

350816.title: Recursive classification of DAGs with toric vanishing ideals by gluing operations
350816.statement: Let $G$ be a directed acyclic graph (DAG) with toric vanishing ideal $I_G$. The relevant constructions are safe gluing, gluing at sinks, and adding a sink. **Recursive classification conjecture.** At least one of the following holds: $G$ is a complete DAG; $G$ is obtained by safe gluing or gluing at sinks of two smaller DAGs with toric vanishing ideals; or $G$ is obtained by adding a sink to a smaller DAG with a toric vanishing ideal. This is the paper's second main conjecture and remains open; it gives the explicit recursive form of the broader constructive classification claim.

350862.title: The shifted reverse Bessel polynomial Hankel-total positivity conjecture
350862.statement:
Let $\mathsf{M}(r,s,\mu,y)$ be the multivariate matrix in the source, and define

$$
\mathsf{M}'(r,s,\mu,y)=\mathsf{M}(r,s,\mu,y)\operatorname{diag}(((rs\mu)^{n(n-1)/2})_{n\geq0}).
$$

Let $\mathsf{M}'_0(x;r,s,\mu,y)=1$ and $\mathsf{M}'_n(x;r,s,\mu,y)=\sum_{k=0}^n m'_{n,k}(r,s,\mu,y)x^k$ for $n>0$. **The shifted reverse Bessel polynomial conjecture.** The sequence $(\mathsf{M}'_n(x;r+1,s+1,\mu+1,y))_{n\geq0}$ is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive jointly in $r,s,\mu,x,y$. This generalizes the known reverse Bessel specialization and is motivated by the failure of the unmodified multivariate sequence; the shifted assertion remains open.

350880.title: Kamatchi–Arumugam tree characterization conjecture for distance-antimagic trees
350880.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree. A tree is **distance antimagic** if it admits a bijection $f:V(T)\to\{1,2,\ldots,|V(T)|\}$ whose vertex weights

$$
w(v)=\sum_{u\in N(v)}f(u)
$$

are distinct. A support vertex is a vertex adjacent to at least one leaf.

**Kamatchi–Arumugam tree conjecture.** $T$ is distance antimagic if and only if every support vertex $v$ has precisely one leaf adjacent to $v$.

The source explicitly describes this as one of the conjectures put forward by Kamatchi and Arumugam and says that these conjectures were yet open. It gives a proposed structural characterization of distance-antimagic trees.

350919.title: The Stanley–Schwartz–Zaks conjecture on distinguishing trees by their chromatic symmetric functions
350919.statement:
Let $T$ and $T'$ be trees, and call them **non-isomorphic** when they do not become the same graph after removing vertex labels. The chromatic symmetric function of a graph $G$ is denoted by $X(G;\mathbf{x})$. **Stanley–Schwartz–Zaks conjecture.** If $T$ and $T'$ are non-isomorphic trees, then

$$
X(T;\mathbf{x})\neq X(T';\mathbf{x}).
$$

This conjecture asks whether the chromatic symmetric function distinguishes all trees up to isomorphism, even though the ordinary chromatic polynomial does not. It is commonly known as the tree-isomorphism conjecture for chromatic symmetric functions and remains open in general.

350924.title: Elementary equivalence from isomorphic cores for graph products
350924.statement:
Let $\mathcal G=\mathcal G(\Gamma,\{G_v\}_{v\in\Gamma})$ and $\mathcal G'=\mathcal G(\Delta,\{G'_v\}_{v\in\Delta})$ be graph products with finite graphs, where each vertex group satisfies a simple non-generic almost positive sentence. **Core converse conjecture.** If there is an isomorphism

$$
f:\operatorname{Core}(\Gamma)\to\operatorname{Core}(\Delta)
$$

and $G_v\equiv G'_{f(v)}$, then

$$
\mathcal G\equiv\mathcal G'.
$$

In particular, each such graph product should be elementarily equivalent to the graph product on its core.

350926.title: Elementary classification by cores for graph products in the specified classes
350926.statement:
Let $\mathcal G(\Gamma,\{G_v\}_{v\in\Gamma})$ and $\mathcal G(\Gamma',\{G'_v\}_{v\in\Gamma'})$ belong to the specified class $\mathcal G(\mathbf F_N,\mathbf C^r_\Phi)$ with $N>0$. Assume either that $\Phi$ consists only of nontrivial positive sentences and the graphs are positive reduced, or that $\Phi$ consists of non-generic almost positive sentences and the graphs are almost positive reduced. **Graph-product core classification conjecture.** Then

$$
\mathcal G(\Gamma,\{G_v\}_{v\in\Gamma})\equiv\mathcal G(\Gamma',\{G'_v\}_{v\in\Gamma'})
$$

if and only if there is an isomorphism

$$
f:\operatorname{Core}(\Gamma)\to\operatorname{Core}(\Gamma')
$$

and $G_v\equiv G'_{f(v)}$. This would extend the RAAG core principle to the indicated classes of graph products.
